transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-18
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Dana (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Ellen (Silverline Procurement), Rajiv (Silverline CISO), Lena (Silverline Legal), Tom (Silverline Platform)

Summary:
Quick procurement/legal review of MSA/DPA and SLAs, discuss security artifacts (SOC2/ISO/KMS), clarify data residency and encryption, confirm pricing tiers and PO workflow, agree next steps for redlines and signature timeline.

Topics:
- MSA & DPA redlines
- SLA targets and remedies (uptime/latency credits)
- Security artifacts (SOC 2, ISO, penetration test reports)
- Data residency and VPC/private deployment options
- Pricing approvals, committed spend, invoicing, PO flow

Transcript:
[00:00] Dana: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, looks like we have all the key folks, cool. um quick agenda, legal + procurement items then q&a, we'll note action items at the end.
[00:20] Ellen: Thanks Dana, yeah procurement side, we just need to make sure the MSA and DPA align with our vendor policy, also need clarity on SLAs and financial remedies, and — and the security docs.
[00:35] Dana: Totally, yeah we'll walk through the redlines we saw and note where Redwood can be flexible. Marcus is on for the security and deployment bits.
[00:45] Marcus: Hey all, hi, so from a security side we'll try to be as transparent as possible, we can provide SOC 2 type II, ISO attestation, pen test summary, and a KMS integration diagram. Some of the language in DPA around key management is... typical stuff but we can discuss.
[01:05] Rajiv: Great. On keys, we require customer-managed keys for PHI workloads, ideally HSM-backed. Does Redwood support external KMS/HSM?
[01:20] Marcus: Yes, we support customer KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK) and we have HSM options for private deployments. For hosted we do envelope encryption and can accept customer-managed keys for customer-specific buckets.
[01:45] Lena: On the MSA we have a redline on indemnity and liability caps, also need stricter audit log retention language and e-discovery support.
[02:05] Dana: Understood. Our standard cap is 1x annual spend, but we do have enterprise negotiation room, depending on committed spend. We can flag that for legal to respond to your redline.
[02:25] Ellen: Timeline wise, procurement needs the final pricing and MSA by next week to make the August purchase window.
[02:40] Dana: Ok we'll prioritize that. Marcus, can you confirm SOC 2 availability and where to share?
[02:50] Marcus: Yep, I will upload SOC 2 type II report and ISO certificate to the secure share, and I'll include a redacted pen test summary. Expect that by Friday.
[03:05] Tom: A question from platform side — what are the Private options? We have some EU-only datasets so we need residency and VPC peering.
[03:20] Marcus: For EU residency we can deploy in a EU region and offer a Private deployment (VPC) with customer-managed networking. For on-prem we have an appliance package but that tends to be a longer timeline.
[03:40] Rajiv: SLA — we need to understand latency SLOs for inference and any credits for missed SLOs. Also curious about fallbacks if a region has an outage.
[03:55] Dana: We publish per-model latency profiles. For enterprise we offer SLA-backed uptime targets, and our fallback policy can route to an alternate region or a compatible model variant. Remedies vary by license tier — we'll include the specific SLA matrix in the package.
[04:20] Lena: Also, we need explicit contractual language on data deletion upon contract termination and proof of deletion.
[04:35] Marcus: We support deletion APIs and can provide attestation logs. For Private deployments we can also provide a snapshot of destroyed key material procedures.
[04:50] Ellen: Pricing — can you walk us through committed spend discounts and invoicing cadence? We prefer net-30 invoicing and a PO process.
[05:05] Dana: Sure. Our pricing sheet has three committed tiers with discounts at 100K, 250K, and 500K annual spend. We can do net-30 invoicing and accept PO. For Dedicated Reserved capacity there are monthly commits. I'll attach the pricing sheet after the call.
[05:25] Ellen: Does Redwood require any deposits for reserved capacity?
[05:35] Dana: For Dedicated we usually require a minimum monthly commit; deposit depends on the contract length. We'll put options in the pricing doc.
[05:50] Rajiv: On compliance artifacts — will you share SOC 2 table of controls mapping? That makes our review quicker.
[06:05] Marcus: Yes, I can include the SOC 2 controls mapping and our security addendum.
[06:20] Lena: A small point — we need SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning for roles, and RBAC controls.
[06:35] Dana: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM; RBAC is supported via our Console. I'll have Marcus include the integration guide.
[06:50] Tom: Any hard dependencies on specific cloud providers for Private? We prefer Azure for our EU stack.
[07:05] Marcus: We support deployments on AWS, GCP, and Azure for Private. There are small differences in networking setup but we have runbooks for Azure VNet peering.
[07:30] Ellen: Ok on the MSA redlines — Lena will send a consolidated list today. What's your usual turnaround for legal on redlines?
[07:45] Dana: Typically 2-3 business days for initial comment; depends on the scope. We'll try to get a redline back quickly since you have an internal window.
[08:00] Lena: We'll flag non-negotiables like data residency, deletion, and indemnity.
[08:10] Dana: Fair. On the SLA credits question — our general approach is service credits calculated as a percentage of monthly fees; exact formula in the SLA.
[08:25] Rajiv: For our security board we'll need to run a short benchmark — latency and token cost estimates on your hosted offering. Can Redwood run a small benchmark for us?
[08:40] Marcus: Yes, we can do a targeted benchmark against your typical payloads. We'll need sample prompts and expected concurrency. If you prefer, a short POC on Dedicated test node is also possible.
[09:00] Ellen: Procurement will need vendor questionnaire answers and our standard HIPAA addendum if any PHI is expected.
[09:15] Marcus: We can fill out vendor questionnaires; HIPAA — we have HIPAA supporting contracts for covered use cases, we'll highlight how data is handled.
[09:30] Dana: Recap — Dana to send redlined MSA & DPA, Marcus SOC2+ISO, pricing sheet; Lena to send consolidated redlines; Ellen to confirm PO approver and timeline. Schedule follow-up call to sign.
[09:50] Lena: Quick clarifying question, on data retention for logs — how long do you keep request logs by default?
[10:05] Marcus: Default is 90 days for request logs; can be configured for enterprise longer retention. We also have options to disable retention for certain routes.
[10:20] Ellen: That helps. On the PO — any specific billing entity name we should put on the PO?
[10:30] Dana: I'll include our billing entity in the pricing doc, and we can accept invoices to Redwood Inference, Inc. with net-30.
[10:40] Rajiv: If we need customer-managed keys for PHI, is there an additional security review?
[10:50] Marcus: There's a short integration checklist and a security review; usually a couple of days. We'll add that to the action items.
[11:05] Dana: Any other blockers?
[11:15] Ellen: Not from procurement, just need the redlines and pricing quickly.
[11:25] Lena: Legal will review once we have Redwood's redline and SOC 2.
[11:35] Tom: Platform will validate the VNet peering doc once it's shared.
[11:45] Dana: Great. We'll aim to get the materials to you by Friday.

[40:00] (jump forward — clarifications on cost alignment and fallback policies)
[41:10] Dana: On fallback policies — we can provide a runbook that shows routing to an alternate region and model variant mapping for graceful degradation.
[42:00] Rajiv: Ok good, please include that in the security packet.
[43:15] Marcus: noted, will include routing and KV cache behavior notes.

[50:00] Dana: Final recap: action items noted, Dana will email redlined agreement and pricing, Marcus will upload security docs, Lena will send redlines, Ellen will confirm PO approver and timeline. Aim to reconvene for signature call week of 2026-08-24.
[50:30] Ellen: Thanks all.
[50:35] Rajiv: Thanks.
[50:40] Lena: Bye.
[50:41] Marcus: Thanks everyone.
[50:45] Dana: Bye!

Links/Artifacts referenced:
- Redlined MSA (to be shared)
- DPA template (Redwood standard)
- SOC 2 Type II report (to be uploaded)
- Pricing sheet (committed tiers + Dedicated options)
- Private deployment runbook (Azure VNet peering doc)

End of transcript.
